passages.title: Every Teenager Should Learn to Cook
text: Many teenagers today can order food with a few taps on their phones, but very few of them can cook a simple meal. In my opinion, learning to cook is one of the most useful skills a teenager can have, and every young person should learn it before leaving home.

The first reason is health. Food from restaurants and food stalls often contains a lot of oil, salt, and sugar. When we cook for ourselves, we can choose fresh ingredients and control how much oil and salt we use. A study by a university in Yogyakarta found that students who cooked at least three times a week ate more vegetables than students who did not.

Second, cooking saves money. A plate of fried rice from a delivery app can cost three or four times more than the same dish made at home, especially after delivery fees are added. Students who live away from their families, for example in boarding houses, can save a large part of their monthly allowance if they prepare their own meals.

Finally, cooking teaches important life skills. To cook a meal, we must plan what to buy, follow steps in the right order, manage time, and clean up afterwards. These skills are also needed at school and at work. Cooking for family or friends can also be a way to show care and to spend time together.

For these reasons, it is clear that cooking is not just a hobby. It is a basic skill that helps teenagers become healthier, more independent, and more responsible. Parents and schools should give young people more chances to practise it.

passages.title: Our Cities Need Better Public Transport
text: Every morning, millions of people in Indonesian cities spend hours stuck in traffic. The air is full of smoke, and people arrive at work and school already tired. I believe that the best way to solve this problem is to improve public transport.

First of all, good public transport can reduce traffic jams. One bus can carry around sixty passengers, while sixty people driving alone would need sixty cars. When buses and trains are fast, safe, and comfortable, more people will leave their cars and motorbikes at home, and the roads will become less crowded.

In addition, public transport is better for the environment. Vehicles are one of the main sources of air pollution in big cities. Fewer private vehicles on the road means less smoke and cleaner air. Electric buses, which some cities have started to use, produce no exhaust gas at all.

Moreover, public transport helps people who do not own a vehicle. Students, older people, and low-income workers depend on buses and trains to reach schools, hospitals, and workplaces. When public transport is cheap and reliable, they have the same opportunities as people who can afford their own vehicles.

Of course, building a good transport system is expensive and takes many years. However, the cost of doing nothing is even higher: wasted time, polluted air, and unhealthy citizens. Therefore, governments should make public transport a top priority.

passages.title: Reading Fiction Makes Us Better People
text: Some people think that reading novels and short stories is a waste of time. They say that students should only read textbooks and practical books that help them get good grades or good jobs. However, I strongly believe that reading fiction is valuable because it makes us better people.

The most important reason is that fiction helps us understand other people. When we read a story, we see the world through the eyes of a character who may be very different from us. We feel their fear, hope, and sadness. Psychologists call this ability empathy, and several studies have shown that people who read fiction regularly score higher on empathy tests.

Fiction also improves our language. Novels contain a wide range of words and sentence patterns that we rarely meet in everyday conversations. Readers learn these words naturally from the story, without memorizing lists. This is why students who read for pleasure often write better essays.

Furthermore, reading fiction is a healthy way to relax. In a world full of notifications and short videos, getting lost in a good book gives our minds a rest. Many readers say that reading for even twenty minutes before bed helps them sleep better.
In short, fiction is not just entertainment. It builds empathy, enriches our language, and helps us rest. Students should be encouraged to put down their phones and pick up a good story.

passages.title: Financial Literacy Should Be Taught at School
text: Many students leave school knowing how to solve complicated equations but not how to manage their own money. In my opinion, financial literacy should be a regular part of the school curriculum.

First, money management is a skill that every person needs. Adults must decide how much to save, how to pay bills, and when to borrow. Without any training, they may make costly mistakes. A recent survey by a financial authority found that fewer than half of young Indonesians could correctly explain what interest is.

Second, young people today face financial temptations earlier than previous generations. Online shops, game purchases, and 'buy now, pay later' apps make spending very easy. A teenager who has never learned to compare prices or to separate wants from needs may fall into debt before reaching adulthood.

Third, learning to save early brings long-term benefits. If a student puts aside even a small amount each month, the habit will grow into a safety net for emergencies and a source of funds for education or a small business.

Some people argue that parents, not schools, should teach children about money. However, not every family has the knowledge or the time to do so, and schools can give equal lessons to all students. For these reasons, I strongly believe that financial literacy deserves a place in our classrooms.
